evals.prompt: I have a talk next week about AI-assisted development. Help me build the presentation.
evals.expected_output: Agent follows Michal's workshop method — starts with premise/framing before jumping to slides.

assertions.name: starts-with-premise
assertions.description: Response begins with premise exploration (what's the core argument?) before creating any slides

assertions.name: follows-workshop-phases
assertions.description: Response follows the phase sequence: premise, framing, draft, polish — not jumping straight to content

assertions.name: includes-opening-and-closing
assertions.description: Response addresses opening hook and closing call-to-action as distinct steps

evals.prompt: Just write me 10 slides about AI tools. Skip the workshop stuff.
evals.expected_output: Agent pushes back on skipping the premise/framing phases — those determine whether the talk lands.

assertions.name: resists-skipping-premise
assertions.description: Response explains why premise/framing matter and doesn't just produce 10 slides

assertions.name: asks-about-audience
assertions.description: Response asks about audience and context before producing content

evals.prompt: The slides are done. I think I'm ready for the talk.
evals.expected_output: Agent reminds about practice step — slides done doesn't mean prepared.

assertions.name: includes-practice-step
assertions.description: Response reminds that practice/rehearsal is part of the preparation process

assertions.name: offers-voice-practice
assertions.description: Response offers voice-powered practice mode if VoiceLayer is available
